Joint graphical lasso

Source: R/jgl.R
jgl.Rd

Fits the joint graphical lasso (JGL) of Danaher, Wang & Witten (2014): K precision matrices estimated together with a lasso penalty on each and a fused or group penalty across them. This is a reimplementation of JGL::JGL() (JGL 2.3.2, archived from CRAN in 2025) with the same arguments, defaults and return value, using the C++ ADMM that ssjgl uses for its M-step. It reproduces JGL::JGL() to numerical precision (see the package tests).

Usage

jgl(
  Y,
  penalty = "fused",
  lambda1,
  lambda2,
  rho = 1,
  weights = "equal",
  penalize.diagonal = FALSE,
  maxiter = 500,
  tol = 1e-05,
  warm = NULL,
  return.whole.theta = FALSE,
  screening = "fast",
  truncate = 1e-05
)

Arguments

Y

List of K data matrices (n_k x p), same variables in the same column order. Each column is centred.

penalty

"fused" (default) or "group".

lambda1

Lasso penalty: a scalar or a symmetric p x p matrix.

lambda2

Fused or group penalty: a scalar or a symmetric p x p matrix.

rho

ADMM step size. Default 1.

weights

"equal" (default; \(w_k = 1\)), "sample.size" (\(w_k = n_k / \sum n_k\)), or a numeric vector of length K.

penalize.diagonal

Logical. Whether the lasso penalty applies to the diagonal (and, for the group penalty, the group penalty too). Default FALSE.

maxiter

Maximum ADMM iterations per block. Default 500.

tol

ADMM convergence tolerance. Default 1e-5.

warm

Optional list of K p x p warm-start precision matrices.

return.whole.theta

Logical. If TRUE, theta holds the full p x p matrices; if FALSE (default), only the connected variables, with the unconnected ones' diagonal entries in theta.unconnected.

screening

Only "fast" is supported. (JGL's "memory.efficient" option gives the same estimates with less memory.)

truncate

Off-diagonal entries with absolute value below this are set to 0. Default 1e-5.

Value

An object of class "jgl", as from JGL::JGL(): a list with theta (list of K precision matrices, with variable names, V1, ..., Vp if Y has none), connected (logical vector; FALSE for variables with no edges in any group) and, if return.whole.theta = FALSE, theta.unconnected (list of K vectors, or NULL). Print and plot methods for this class come from the JGL package, if it is loaded.

Details

The objective is $$\sum_k w_k [\mathrm{tr}(S_k\Theta_k) - \log\det\Theta_k] + \lambda_1 \sum_k \sum_{i \ne j} |\theta^{(k)}_{ij}| + P_2(\Theta),$$ where \(S_k\) is the (biased) sample covariance of group k and \(P_2\) is \(\lambda_2 \sum_{k < k'} \sum_{ij} |\theta^{(k)}_{ij} - \theta^{(k')}_{ij}|\) (fused) or \(\lambda_2 \sum_{i \ne j} \sqrt{\sum_k (\theta^{(k)}_{ij})^2}\) (group). As in JGL, the fused penalty also applies to the diagonal, and the lasso penalty applies to the diagonal only if penalize.diagonal = TRUE. The problem is split into independent blocks by JGL's exact screening rule before solving.

References

Danaher, P., Wang, P. and Witten, D. M. (2014). The joint graphical lasso for inverse covariance estimation across multiple classes. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B, 76(2), 373–397. doi:10.1111/rssb.12033

See also

ssjgl() for the spike-and-slab version with adaptive, edge-specific penalties.

Examples

sim <- simulate_ssjgl_data(K = 2, p = 10, n = 100, seed = 1)
fit <- jgl(sim$data_list, penalty = "fused", lambda1 = 0.1, lambda2 = 0.05,
           return.whole.theta = TRUE)
round(fit$theta[[1]][1:4, 1:4], 2)
#>      V1    V2    V3    V4
#> V1 0.92  0.16  0.13  0.00
#> V2 0.16  0.89  0.27 -0.06
#> V3 0.13  0.27  0.80 -0.06
#> V4 0.00 -0.06 -0.06  0.88
# partial correlations, one matrix per group
pc <- lapply(fit$theta, precision_to_pcor)
